harness_surface.guardrails: CLAUDE.md (What this agent does not do) + .claude/settings.json deny
harness_surface.skills: skills/<id>@v<n>/ (SKILL.md, skill.json, scripts/, cases.json), run through src/run_skill.py
harness_surface.session_skills: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md: run-skill, the one that names the runner, with library/index.md and one page per library skill beside it, rendered from the manifests; classify-knowledge; choose-session-level

note: A build copies this tree, fills CLAUDE.md's placeholders, adds tools/<name>/ with adapter.py, tool.json and errors/, fills CAPABILITIES.json and envelope/, writes validation/ and replay/ tasks, copies the skills the specification names into skills/ unchanged, renders .claude/skills/run-skill/library/ from their manifests (index.md and one page per skill) and writes .claude/agents/<name>.md for the subagents it names. The diff from this tree is recorded next to the bundle. v2 added src/run_skill.py and the Subagents section to v1 (meta_agent/tasks/010). v3 adds three session skills (meta_agent/tasks/015; the person, 2026-11-12): run-skill, which sends the bundle's session to src/run_skill.py and says what a session may and may not change, with its library pages; classify-knowledge and choose-session-level, adapted to a bundle from the Meta-Agent's own, naming no path outside the bundle and no script under src/; and in CLAUDE.md the sentences that name them and the rules they repeat. Bundle check B15 judges a bundle of v3 or later. v4 changes text only, after a fresh session was watched in a bundle of v3 (meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261112-meta-macbook-20261112-1-5.json): run-skill also says how a tool that no library skill calls is called, through src/run_tool.py, and its description and CLAUDE.md's sentence for it say so; tasks/001-start.md says that src/validate_tasks.py ends with a failure status when the verdict is undecided and that this is expected; a build with no library skill writes 'no library skill' where it wrote 'no skills'. v5 changes text only, after a fresh session was watched in a copy of a bundle of v4 outside the repository (meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261113-meta-macbook-20261112-1-1.json, answered in meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261113-design-macbook-20261112-1-1.json): tasks/001-start.md covers a scientific verdict of not_run as well as undecided; CLAUDE.md says that envelope/safety.json holds one entry per safety value and that a file with none means no tool requires a gate, that the folder named runs is made by the session when it first writes there, and that an input nothing in the bundle gives is one line in failures.jsonl like a missing skill; run-skill has a section for such an input. v6 changes text and no script, after two fresh sessions worked in copies of bundles of v5 in a test run outside the repository (meta_agent/tasks/016; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261116-design-macbook-20261116-1-2.json): CLAUDE.md names README.md, TEMPLATE.json and CAPABILITIES.json and says what a claim with not_here is; it says that the runner of skills writes a record only with --record and that the runner of tools writes none, what the status each runner and each check ends with means, that the three checks are not tool calls, that a replay item made by hand is still compared by src/replay.py, and which keys a line of failures.jsonl has; and it says that a grade is the builder's and is not derived here. The bundle carries no grade table: deriving a grade is a calculation, a calculation in a bundle is a library skill, and the library has none for it, so a table without the skill would be read by hand. run-skill repeats the procedure for a record, for a kept output and for a replay item. From this version the builder writes the unit a tool contract names into the Tools section, writes CAPABILITIES.json with the name of the document it read and not its path in the builder's tree, marks a claim that names a tool the bundle does not carry, and lists what is held. Bundle check B16 judges a bundle of this version or later. Every earlier version stays under templates/. v7 changes one script and no text, after a session of a test run built the first agent on an engine (meta_agent/tasks/016; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261116-design-macbook-20261116-1-8.json): src/validate_tasks.py also judges a scientific task whose reference is what a source states, which the task carries as measure.stated, a map from an output field to the stated value, beside the reference that names the source; nothing is computed, and the agreement is the largest absolute difference, judged against the person's tolerance as before. One tolerance has one unit, so several stated fields are judged together only by an exact tolerance, and otherwise the task is undecided and says to state one field per task. A call that was not made is not_run and not a failure: the gate refused it, a permission was missing, or what the tool needs was not there. A task with a reference function is judged as before. v8 changes the gate and the sentences about it, after the person's word of 2026-11-16 that an engine tool opens by the lab's execution permission (meta_agent/tasks/016; docs/ideas/20261116.md; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261116-design-macbook-20261116-1-9.json): src/gate.py opens a tool whose contract says safety_gate.opens_by execution_permission, and whose side effects are runs_process or writes_files, where envelope/execution_permission.json is a level a person confirmed that reaches engine or instrument; it refuses such a tool otherwise with a refused_by_safety error that names the level it found, and every other gated tool still opens only by safety values a person wrote. The self-check also says when the permission file is not a person's. CLAUDE.md says what opens each gate and names the file as one a session never writes; run-skill does not name it, since a bundle without such a tool carries no such file (check 24). The builder writes the file from the lab profile a build names, and none where the profile carries the permission only as words. v9 changes the gate, CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json, after round three of the clone test built an agent on an engine whose environment no tool of the bundle could make, though the person had allowed pixi from conda-forge (meta_agent/tasks/016; docs/ideas/20261116.md; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261116-design-macbook-20261116-1-10.json): src/gate.py lets a tool that reaches the network run only as an install, where its contract names installs_from {installer, channel}, its gate opens by the execution permission, the permission reaches engine or instrument and lists that pair under package_sources; it refuses every other network tool with refused_by_safety, code GATE-NETWORK-001, whatever its contract asks of the gate. CLAUDE.md says this is the one network call the agent may make; .claude/settings.json denies a session's edit of envelope/execution_permission.json as it does that of envelope/safety.json. The builder copies package_sources from the lab profile into that file. v10 changes text, the runner of tools and nothing of the gate, after round four's bundle on an engine was tested standing alone (meta_agent/tasks/016; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261117-design-macbook-20261116-1-1.json): README.md names .claude/agents/ only where a bundle has subagents, and names the permission file and runs/; CLAUDE.md says which file opens which gate and that an empty envelope/safety.json means no tool opens by safety values, that a tool which writes files, and the checks that call it, leave folders under runs/, that the install keeps its package cache in runs/cache, and that a value a run measured is reported with its grade not derived, the grade being derived where the Meta-Agent takes the report into a record; tasks/001-start.md quotes the last line each of the first two checks prints; src/run_tool.py points the package caches of pixi, pip, uv and conda, and the cache root, at runs/cache before the install the gate opens, and refuses an output whose field of unit count is below zero. v11 changes text and the runner of tools and nothing of the gate, after round five's bundle on an engine was tested standing alone (meta_agent/tasks/016; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261117-design-macbook-20261116-1-4.json). Every path this note names under docs/, meta_agent/ or contracts/ is a record of the builder's repository and is not in this bundle; the reason for each version is said in this note in its own words. CLAUDE.md says that such a path is not looked for and that the builder marks every task and replay item that names one with builder_records, quoting a person's words where it had them; it has a Workflow section the build fills with the order in which the workflow calls the tools, or says that the request gave none; and it says that the install never installs its installer. tasks/001-start.md says that a scientific not_run for want of an engine's environment is followed by the agent's own install and a second run of src/validate_tasks.py. src/run_tool.py looks for the installer a contract names on PATH before the install and, where it is not there, returns an unavailable error that names it and says that putting it there is the person's step. v12 changes text only, on the person's word of 2026-11-17 that a quantity entering a card or a decision is a library skill and a value the engine reports is read (docs/ideas/20261117.md; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261117-design-macbook-20261116-1-8.json): CLAUDE.md has a Decisions section that says a run-time decision is taken by a diagnostic library skill on a criterion a row hands it, undecided and the person's where the row is null, and that the build fills with each decision the request names: the diagnostic skill, the tool output it judges and the row that hands each criterion; the Procedure says that a value a tool's output reports is read from it and not computed again. v13 changes one script and no text, after the clone of run 20261117-3 built an agent whose scientific tasks measure through a library skill (meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261117-design-macbook-20261116-1-10.json; the intake's analysis, 23bb51b): src/validate_tasks.py runs a scientific task's analysis, handing the call's output field to the skill's input and each other input from its row of envelope/parameters.json, through src/run_skill.py, and judges the skill's named output against the reference; a row that is absent or null leaves the task not_run. v14 changes text only, after the Meep bundle was tested standing alone (meta_agent/tasks/021; meta_agent/failures.jsonl em-7, em-8, em-9) and the Quantum ESPRESSO bundle beside it (dft-5): CLAUDE.md says that the builder also marks a card of its repository named by its id and a question it put to the person named by its number, envelope/parameters.json among the files it marks, quoting the question and any answer; tasks/001-start.md says that before the install an interface task whose call starts the engine fails for want of the environment as a scientific task is not_run, and that the verdict after the install is the one that says whether the interface works. From this version the builder refuses an optional input of a tool contract that names neither a row nor a default, and writes a default into the Tools section. v15 changes the gate, the runner of tools and CLAUDE.md, after round two of the Quantum ESPRESSO test built an agent that held its fetch tools for want of a way to read data from hosts the person had allowed (meta_agent/tasks/023; meta_agent/failures.jsonl dft-7; docs/ideas/20261117.md): src/gate.py opens a tool that reaches the network as an install, as a read of data, or as both, where its gate opens by the execution permission and the permission reaches engine or instrument. A read of data is a tool whose contract names fetches_from, a list of {host, access}, every one of which the permission lists under data_sources with the same access, a host matched by equality. An install and a read are each judged against their own list: data_sources never opens an install and package_sources never opens a read; a network tool that names neither is refused, code GATE-NETWORK-001, and the refusal names both lists. src/run_tool.py looks for an installer and points the package caches at runs/cache only for a tool that names installs_from. CLAUDE.md says which network calls the agent may make. The builder copies data_sources from the lab profile into envelope/execution_permission.json as it copies package_sources. v16 changes one script of the checks, the runner of tools and text, after the CFD test's clone and its bundle standing alone (meta_agent/tasks/019; meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-2, cfd-7, cfd-10, cfd-11; dft-2): src/validate_tasks.py takes a scientific task's agreement from the library skill this file names under agreement_skill, through src/run_skill.py, for each stated field and for a reference function alike, judges the magnitude it gives against the person's tolerance and prints each run; a bundle without the skill fails the task and says so. The builder puts that skill into every bundle with a scientific task. A tool may ship several error contracts of one category: the first is errors/<category>.json and is the one src/run_tool.py returns itself, each other errors/<category>.<code>.json, so that no contract of the intake is lost. tasks/001-start.md says that a replay item whose call starts the engine fails before the install as an interface task does, and that replay is run again after it, and that its Status line is the builder's; CLAUDE.md says that a task's Status line is the builder's, that the dates the builder wrote are in UTC, and that the agreement is the skill's output. v17 changes the runner of tools, after round two of the CFD test met a contract whose input type is a list (meta_agent/tasks/019; meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-13): src/run_tool.py takes a JSON-Schema type that is a list of types, such as an integer or null, accepts a value of any of them and checks it further as the one it is, and refuses a value of none of them with an invalid_input error contract; it took such a list as one type name and raised before. From this version the builder also keeps on the validation report each run of the agreement skill, as a number whose source names the skill and the task (src/validate/gate.py, cfd-14). v18 changes text only, the bundle's classify-knowledge, so that it says what the builder's own says (the design role's ask 20261117-design-macbook-20261117-1-14 on the person's decision of 2026-11-17, meta_agent/failures.jsonl em-10; and cfd-5, cfd-16 of meta_agent/tasks/019): spec is the maker's documentation, a vendor's specification, a manual, or a tutorial or example page of the engine's or instrument's maker; a quantity defined only up to a constant is compared with another only after both share its zero; and a value a source tabulates from its own raw series is read against that series where the source publishes it. v19 changes one script of the checks and the start task, on the person's standing rule of 2026-11-18 for scientific tolerances (the design role's ask 20261118-design-macbook-20261117-1-5): src/validate_tasks.py judges a scientific task by a tolerance chosen by a person or by one derived by that rule (chosen_by rule, with the rule, the skill that derived it and which way it came), alike, and by no other; tasks/001-start.md says so and that a session sets neither. From this version the builder derives such a tolerance, where the person gave none, by the library skill this file names under tolerance_rule, through the runner, from the reference as its task prints it (bundle.py). v20 changes one script of the checks, on the person's word of 2026-11-18 that every simulation bundle carries a common set of library skills made in advance, adapted to its engine during the build (docs/ideas/20261118.md; meta_agent/tasks/025): this file names the set under common_skills, and the builder puts each into every bundle whose tool is an engine, unless its specification names a version of that skill already; a build that adapts one to its engine carries the adapted next version in its place (adapted_from, its engine named), and the difference from this template lists it. src/validate_tasks.py takes the agreement skill's name from this file, now measurement_error@v2, the common version; the error-range skill of the rule is tolerance_from_reference@v2. The agreement skill is not adapted. v21 changes this file alone: the common set also carries discretization_error_from_two_resolutions@v1, the run's own numerical error from two resolutions by generalized Richardson extrapolation, which the person's amended tolerance rule weighs ('Yes, run's own error', docs/ideas/20261118.md; meta_agent/tasks/025). v22 changes one script of the checks, after round three of the CFD test met the person's tolerances given as intervals (meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-19; the report's schema at eb41e50): src/validate_tasks.py judges a tolerance {interval: {low, high}, unit, chosen_by human, source} by whether the measured value lies within the interval, its edges as written, through the diagnostic skill this file names under interval_skill, run by src/run_skill.py on a series of that one value with a window of one; within is a pass, below or above a fail, and the run is printed with the task. The builder carries that skill into every bundle with such a task. v23 changes one script of the checks, on the person's words of 2026-11-18 ('Yes, refine and derive') and the intake card's scientific_tasks[].refinement (32684cc): a scientific task that names a refinement, and has no tolerance a person gave, is judged by the tolerance the standing rule derives from the run's own numerical error: src/validate_tasks.py makes the call as built and again with the finer inputs the refinement's rows hand it, runs the refinement's skill on the two through src/run_skill.py for the finer result's error, and the rule's skill (tolerance_rule) on that error, and judges the finer result by it, chosen_by rule, from run_numerical_error; the record names the inputs refined, so a refinement of the time step alone says it measures the temporal part only. Where the finer run or the estimate cannot be made, the half-digit branch alone applies and the record says the run's error was not estimated. The builder carries both skills into such a bundle. From v24 the rule's skill is tolerance_from_reference@v3 and is handed how the run's error was estimated, read off run_error_from by the refinement's skill: a two-grid estimate enters three times over (the person, 2026-11-18, 'Yes, factor 3'), and the record names it. v25 changes one script of the checks and this file, after round four of the CFD test found no source for the scheme's order (meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-25) and the intake card took third_inputs (6c7a488): a refinement that names a third, finer run makes it, observes the order from the three results by the skill this file names under order_skill, through src/run_skill.py, estimates the finest result's error from the two finest at that order and judges the finest; the rule's skill is told three_or_more_grids, so that no factor enters (the person, 2026-11-18). Where no order can be read the half-digit branch applies and the record says why. The common set also carries observed_order_of_convergence@v1. v26 changes one script of the checks and this file, after round four of the rheoTool test met a reference the guide gives exactly, the centreline velocity as three halves of the mean, to which half a printed digit lent a tolerance the run did not earn (meta_agent/failures.jsonl rheotool-11, rheotool-28; the design role's reply f071852): a scientific task marks such a reference exact (measure.exact, the stated field to true), src/validate_tasks.py hands the mark to the rule's skill, now tolerance_from_reference@v4, and the half-digit branch does not apply to it, so the run's own error alone gives the tolerance, with the same factors; with no run error estimated the task stays undecided. A task that marks nothing is judged as under v25. v27 changes the gate, one script of the checks, .claude/settings.json and text, after rounds three to five of the rheoTool test (meta_agent/failures.jsonl rheotool-22, rheotool-23, rheotool-29, rheotool-32): src/gate.py reads CAPABILITIES.json and opens an install from a pair the lab's permission allows for named engines alone only in a bundle whose engine is one of them, as the builder's check B9 does (the person, 2026-11-18, 'Yes, covered'); src/validate_tasks.py prints under each scientific task the tolerance that judged it, with its unit and how it came, the agreement where a reason took its place, and the run's own error with how it was estimated and its factor, which were in --json alone, and its docstring names the agreement skill by this file and not as measurement_error@v1; the PostToolUse hook runs the gate's self-check by the project's path, so that it runs from any working directory; and the common set carries series_settled@v4, which says undecided for a window no row gives, where v3 raised.
